item.text: Verification is clean. I’m pulling exact line references for the new scenario structure and the simplified consumer code, then I’ll summarize the maintainability gains.

Refactored the scenario model so search expectations are now represented as one ordered concept instead of two parallel collections. [BTreeScenario.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTreeScenario.java:5) now stores a single `List<SearchExpectation>` alongside the inserted keys and derived traversal, with small factory methods for `present(...)` and `missing(...)`. That makes each fixture self-contained and removes the old split between “present keys” and “missing keys,” which was a weaker representation of the same idea.

That change simplified the consumers as well. [BTreeSamples.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTreeSamples.java:2) now defines scenarios in a more linear form, [BTreeTestSupport.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTreeTestSupport.java:35) validates search behavior by iterating one expectation list, and [Main.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/Main.java:8) prints the demo results from that same source. The result is less branching and fewer ways for fixture data to drift.

Verified with `javac BTree.java BTreeScenario.java BTreeSamples.java BTreeTestSupport.java BTreeTest.java Main.java`, `java -cp . Main`, and `java -cp . BTreeTest`.
